Forecast Discussion

High pressure slips off the coast today. A southwest flow keeps the afternoon mild.

A cold front crosses the mountains Thursday morning. A few showers arrive after midnight tonight, and mostly light showers remain possible Thursday, especially on the west side of the Appalachians.

A secondary front arrives Thursday evening on gusty northwest winds. Sharply colder air follows. Showers change to snow showers from west to east Thursday night.

Friday is cold and windy. Snow showers and flurries favor the west edge of the Appalachians. A third surge of energy Friday evening carries light accumulating snow farther east. Snow showers and flurries taper off Saturday morning.

Accumulations focus along the western escarpment and the higher elevations, with little or none in the eastern third of the mountain region. Here is our preliminary snowfall map. Don’t take it literally, but a picture is worth a thousand words.

High pressure settles overhead Sunday. The morning is cold; the afternoon recovers under sunshine.

Early next week, high pressure moves to the Mid-Atlantic as low pressure tracks along the Gulf Coast. For now, I kept Monday night and Tuesday dry. A cool northeast flow may hold Tuesday’s temperatures down. We do have some uncertainty about the northern extent of rain reaching us. Even a touch of snow is not out of the question.
